title: Choose the composition of the chess solving view
question: The world is settled: osm.sh's terminal grammar, rendered light. This round is composition only. The roll dealt these three structures; lock one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Transformation ledger
options.lineage: unified diff output, read in a light terminal
options.thesis: A positional transformation is a diff: every move you play writes a minus and a plus line, and the solved puzzle shows before and after side by side.
options.viewport: Board on the left at full column height, pieces as glyphs on the grid. Right column: the prompt as a comment line at top, then a ledger that fills as you play (‘− Nf3  + Nd5’, opponent replies indented), a wrong move appearing struck through and fading. Status bar across the bottom: puzzle id, move n of m, keys. On solve the ledger collapses and the board splits into before | after with changed squares tinted.
options.risk: Non-programmer friends may read the diff marks as an in-joke; the notation must read as chess first, and the before/after split must be the payoff, not the gimmick.

options.label: Game score column
options.lineage: a chess periodical's printed game score, set on a typewriter
options.thesis: The board sits above a single typewritten score column; your moves and the replies type themselves in, and the annotation appears beneath once the idea is complete.
options.viewport: Prompt as a one-line headnote. Board centered beneath it at generous size. Below the board, a numbered score column (‘1. Nd5  Bxd5  2. exd5’) that fills as you play, with an active-step marker; a replay cursor lets you step back through the line. On solve, the explanation sets in a measured prose column under the score. Status line last.
options.risk: The vertical stack pushes the score and explanation below the fold on a laptop; wrong-move feedback has to live at the board, never down the page.

raised.raise: Every step in the line is recoverable: the score column is a replayable, numbered sequence with one marker on the active step, not a log.

options.label: Bare board
options.lineage: a correspondence chess postcard: position, one line of text, nothing else
options.thesis: Nothing but the board and one status line; prompt above, feedback and progress below, and the explanation arrives as a card only once you have solved it.
options.viewport: The board at the largest size the viewport allows, centered. One line above it carries the prompt. One line below carries state: ‘your move’, ‘not that’, ‘2 of 3’, ‘solved’. On solve, an explanation card slides up from the status line and the board dims behind it.
options.risk: A multi-move sequence has no visible history, and the explanation has nowhere natural to sit without covering the board it explains.

options.label: Fold sequence
options.lineage: orizuru crane fold sequence, thirty-two numbered steps on one sheet
options.thesis: The solve as a numbered fold sequence: one sheet, one marker on the active step, every earlier step recoverable.
options.viewport: Board as the sheet, a strict numbered margin column of steps beside it, one marker on the active step.
options.case: Its step topology fuses cleanly into the score column and is already donated there; on its own it loses narrowly on chess clarity.
options.risk: Read literally it becomes a tutorial stepper, which is not how a puzzle feels.

options.label: ASCII live scene
options.thesis: The whole view is one live glyph grid.
options.viewport: A board rendered as luminance glyphs.
options.case: Its identity is already the committed world; as a structure it adds nothing to the task.
options.kept: The board is text on one grid, selectable, never an image.
options.risk: Pure novelty over a task surface.

options.label: Seven-segment mask
options.thesis: Fixed cells, only which segments light changes.
options.viewport: Move counter as a segment display.
options.case: Loses both axes: nothing in the solve is a numeric readout.
options.kept: Absence drawn deliberately: empty squares and unplayed steps are designed, not blank.

options.label: Ticket wallet
options.case: Loses both axes: friends solving a puzzle do not identify with travel paperwork.
options.kept: Nothing disappears, it cancels: a wrong move stays visible, struck, in the ledger.

options.label: Metro tiles
options.thesis: Type is the interface, tiles are the doors.
options.case: Loses both axes: breaks the monospace grid the brand commits to.
options.kept: Chrome deleted: no borders or button frames the grid does not need.

options.label: Tensegrity column
options.lineage: kinetic tension sculpture with engineering labels
options.thesis: Trace every force to its counterforce.
options.viewport: Pieces as nodes with leader-line annotations.
options.case: Loses both axes: annotating tensions on the board would spoil the puzzle.
options.kept: After solving, the explanation may pin notes to squares with leader lines.
